'''Bodhisattva Sen''' is an Indian-American statistician.

Sen earned his bachelor and master of statistics from the [[Indian Statistical Institute]] in 2002 and 2004, respectively.<ref name="bscolumbia">{{cite news |title=Bodhisattva Sen |url=http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~bodhi/Bodhi/Welcome.html |access-date=13 August 2023 |publisher=Columbia University Department of Statistics}}</ref><ref name="bscv32023">{{cite news |title=Bodhisattva Sen (CV) |url=http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~bodhi/CV/CV.pdf |access-date=13 August 2023 |date=10 March 2023}}</ref> He then completed a doctorate in statistics at the [[University of Michigan]] in the United States.<ref name="bscolumbia"/><ref name="bscv32023"/> Sen's doctoral dissertation, ''A Study of Bootstrap And Likelihood Based Methods In Non-standard Problems'', was published in 2008 and jointly advised by [[Michael Woodroofe]] and [[Moulinath Banerjee]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy}}</ref>

Sen joined the [[Columbia University]] Department of Statistics as an assistant professor in 2008. Sen was successively promoted to an associate professorship in 2013, and a full professorship in 2020.<ref name="bscv32023"/> In 2022, he was elected a fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] for "important contributions to nonparametric inference under shape constraints, optimal transport and its applications to Statistics, and the bootstrap".<ref name="imsfellow">{{cite news |title=2022 IMS Fellows Announced |url=https://imstat.org/2022/04/22/2022-ims-fellows-announced/ |access-date=13 August 2023 |publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |date=22 April 2022}}</ref><ref name="columbiafims">{{cite news |title=Congratulations to Bodhisattva Sen and Tian Zheng on being named 2022 IMS Fellows. |url=https://stat.columbia.edu/2022/04/26/congratulations-to-bodhisattva-sen-and-tian-zheng-on-being-named-2022-ims-fellows/ |access-date=13 August 2023 |publisher=Columbia University Department of Statistics |date=26 April 2022}}</ref>
